{{Short description|Mathematical result in large deviations theory}}
In [[mathematics]], the '''Dawson&ndash;Gärtner theorem''' is a result in [[large deviations theory]].  Heuristically speaking, the Dawson&ndash;Gärtner theorem allows one to transport a [[large deviation principle]] on a “smaller” [[topological space]] to a “larger” one.

==Statement of the theorem==
Let (''Y''<sub>''j''</sub>)<sub>''j''∈''J''</sub> be a [[projective system]] of [[Hausdorff space|Hausdorff topological spaces]] with maps ''p''<sub>''ij''</sub>&nbsp;:&nbsp;''Y''<sub>''j''</sub>&nbsp;→&nbsp;''Y''<sub>''i''</sub>.  Let ''X'' be the projective limit (also known as the inverse limit) of the system (''Y''<sub>''j''</sub>,&nbsp;''p''<sub>''ij''</sub>)<sub>''i'',''j''∈''J''</sub>, i.e.

:<math>X = \varprojlim_{j \in J} Y_{j} = \left\{ \left. y = (y_{j})_{j \in J} \in Y = \prod_{j \in J} Y_{j} \quad \right| \quad i < j \implies y_{i} = p_{ij} (y_{j}) \right\}.</math>

Let (''&mu;''<sub>''&epsilon;''</sub>)<sub>''&epsilon;''&gt;0</sub> be a family of [[probability measure]]s on ''X''.  Assume that, for each ''j''&nbsp;∈&nbsp;''J'', the [[push-forward measure]]s (''p''<sub>''j''∗</sub>''&mu;''<sub>''&epsilon;''</sub>)<sub>''&epsilon;''&gt;0</sub> on ''Y''<sub>''j''</sub> satisfy the large deviation principle with [[good rate function]] ''I''<sub>''j''</sub>&nbsp;:&nbsp;''Y''<sub>''j''</sub>&nbsp;→&nbsp;'''R'''&nbsp;∪&nbsp;{+∞}.  Then the family (''&mu;''<sub>''&epsilon;''</sub>)<sub>''&epsilon;''&gt;0</sub> satisfies the large deviation principle on ''X'' with good rate function ''I''&nbsp;:&nbsp;''X''&nbsp;→&nbsp;'''R'''&nbsp;∪&nbsp;{+∞} given by

:<math>I(x) = \sup_{j \in J} I_{j}(p_{j}(x)).</math>
